name: Emilio Butragueño
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Real Madrid senior debut on 5 February 1984 at age 20, scoring two goals and assisting the third in a 3-2 comeback win over Cádiz; went on to win two consecutive UEFA Cups (1985, 1986) and the Bravo Trophy for best U-24 player in Europe twice.
early_history_summary: Butragueño grew up in Madrid as a Real Madrid supporter — his father was club member #75 — and joined the Real Madrid youth academy in 1981 after initially being rejected. He played for Real Madrid Castilla (reserves) where his prolific scoring attracted attention, leading to his senior debut in February 1984 at age 20. He became the figurehead of the famous 'Quinta del Buitre' generation that dominated Spanish football in the late 1980s.
family_context_summary: Raised in a middle-class Madrid family; his father owned a perfume store off Gran Vía and was a passionate Real Madrid member (member #75 since 1943). Butragueño was registered as a Real Madrid member the day after his birth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Real Madrid member from 1943 and brought Emilio to matches from childhood, embedding deep club affinity and access. Father used contacts within the club to arrange a second youth trial after Emilio was initially rejected.

evidence_summary: Butragueño grew up in a middle-class Madrid household where his father owned a perfume store and was Real Madrid member #75, providing early club immersion. After initially failing Real Madrid's youth trial, his father used club contacts to arrange a second trial in 1981. Emilio starred for Real Madrid Castilla, was called up by Alfredo Di Stéfano in February 1984, and immediately impacted the first team. He became the leader of the 'Quinta del Buitre' — a cohort of young Castilla graduates (Sanchís, Míchel, Martín Vázquez, Pardeza) who transformed Real Madrid in the 1980s, winning two consecutive UEFA Cups by age 23.

Dorothy died in 1983 when Patrick was entering his junior year at Georgetown.
